text: GET /api/recovery/access/v1/role-catalogue/{roleCode} returns roleCode, roleName, roleClass, defaultScope and the matrix version in force for one role code, and 404 when no row is in force or the row is inactive. The authorise call of a next-action read takes the caller identity from the session, the area CASE_RECORD, the right R, the case ID, the case owner, the team code, the queue role and the field IDs DF-CAS-049 to DF-CAS-053, and answers with the decision code (AC-READ or AC-DENY), the scope result, the matrix version, the marker of each field ID and the entry reference. The database login is called 'the rwb-access login (DP-02)'.
why: No source names a role read, and Architecture v5 names the authorise path without a schema, so the two shapes and the login HAVE to be fixed as a default before the build; leaving them empty would stop the story.

text: LOV-ROLE-CLASS carries CUSTOMER_PARTY as a fourth value in the same versioned load that carries the roles, and CU-BORROW carries that class with the name 'Customer (borrower)'. The classes that produce a waiting next action are read from that class value by the next-action caller (legacy BR5), and this service publishes the class and writes no waiting text of its own.
why: The list of role classes has no customer-party value while legacy BR5 and legacy AC3 need one, and the next action of a customer-party owner cannot be classed without a default.

text: The Case record letters of RW-CASEOWN, RW-TEAMMGR, RW-RESTRUCT, RW-COMPLAIN and RW-AUDIT are R with default scope OWN for RW-CASEOWN, TEAM for RW-TEAMMGR and the scope their role row carries for the other three, and RW-REFADM holds no Case record letter; all of them are read from the policy pack as data and none is written in code.
why: The RBAC matrix tabulates three capability areas and no Case record letter, while the next-action read is decided in CASE_RECORD, so the letters and scopes have to be read as data with a default.

text: The role catalogue answer names the matrix version in force as the version of the rows it returned, the answer and the role rows are cached under that version and are dropped in the transaction that publishes rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1, no lifetime clock is configured, and the masking version in force in SIT is MASK-SIT-01.
why: The role table has no version column and no source fixes a cache lifetime, while the answer has to name a version and a policy change has to take effect with no deployment.
